newsitem.title: USA: Pacificare sees Q2 EPS $0.30 to $0.45.
newsitem.headline: Pacificare sees Q2 EPS $0.30 to $0.45.

text.p: Pacificare Health Systems Inc said Friday it expects to report second quarter net income of $0.30 to $0.45 per share, sharply below the $1.15 per share before pre-tax charges in the year-ago quarter.

The company earlier this week had warned of a substantial earnings shortfall in the second quarter, but had not given a specific estimate. It said the forecast issued Friday compared with a consensus analyst estimate of $1.16 per share.
Pacificare also said Friday it expects to report a substantial drop in earnings for the fiscal year ended in December.

The company said the main reason for the earnings shortfall was substantially higher health care costs in a number of markets, mainly those acquired in the $2.2 billion purchase of FHP International Co.
Weakness in PacifiCare operations in California and Oregon markets, and a number of non-recurring expenses for reserve increases and other adjustments were also cited.

PacifiCare said the FHP California operations it acquired in February are performing below expectations, due mainly to a decline in commercial prices in 1996, and are responsible for about 25 percent of the total earnings shortfall expected.
It also said its own operations in California are being hurt by higher than expected prescription drug costs and higher health care costs in its Medicare program.

PacifiCare also forecast a significantly lower membership growth rate this year in both its commercial and Medicare product lines, and said the total medical loss ratio is expected to increase this year.

"We are obviously disappointed by the performance of a number of these newly acquired assets," Alan Hoops, president and chief executive officer said in a statement. He added that the integration of FHP operations is proceeding on schedule and according to plan.

While analysts had already reduced earnings estimates following the warning PacifiCare made earlier in the week, the specific forecast issued Friday appeared to be below even their reduced expectations.
Most analysts had said they expected the shortfall to reduce earnings only by $0.10 to $0.20 per share. First Call on Friday had a consensus estimate of $1.03 per share.
